claims.quote: Storitve računalništva v javno dostopnem oblaku se lahko uporabljajo le za obravnavo informacijskih premoženj, ki niso uvrščena v varnostne razrede ali so uvrščena v varnostne razrede Z1, C1 in R1.
claims.quote_english: Public cloud computing services may be used only for information assets that are not assigned to security classes or are assigned to security classes Z1, C1 and R1.
claims.title: Uredba o informacijski varnosti v državni upravi (Uradni list RS, št. 29/2018), 41. člen

claims.publisher: Ministrstvo za notranje zadeve in javno upravo (GOV.SI)
claims.quote: Na tej infrastrukturi se izvajajo storitve, ki uporabljajo občutljive, osebne in druge podatke in informacije, ki jih država ne želi shranjevati zunaj svojega okolja.
claims.quote_english: This infrastructure runs services that use sensitive, personal and other data and information that the state does not want to store outside its own environment.
claims.title: Informatika v državni upravi

indicators.research_note: The binding Government Decree on Information Security in State Administration (Art. 41) bars public cloud use for information assets in higher security classes (above Z1/C1/R1) and requires ministry approval otherwise; this keeps higher-class data on state infrastructure but is not an explicit national/EU jurisdiction clause for government data generally. The ministry states the state cloud (DRO) hosts data the state does not want stored outside its environment (policy, not statute). No statute found expressly requiring all government data to be stored under Slovenian/EU jurisdiction; hence partial (restriction applies only to classified/higher security classes). The new information security act (NIS2 transposition) was not checked for a localisation clause.

review.reason: Art. 41 of the 2018 Decree is quoted correctly, but it only limits public-cloud use to assets in lower security classes and requires ministry approval; the fetched text sets no national or EU storage or jurisdiction requirement, and the gov.si DRO sentence is a policy statement, not binding law.

claims.quote: STROGO TAJNO, ki se določi za tajne podatke, katerih razkritje nepoklicani osebi bi ogrozilo vitalne interese Republike Slovenije ali jim nepopravljivo škodovalo
claims.quote_english: TOP SECRET, assigned to classified information whose disclosure to an unauthorised person would endanger or irreparably damage the vital interests of the Republic of Slovenia
claims.title: Zakon o tajnih podatkih (uradno prečiščeno besedilo) (ZTP-UPB2), 13. člen

claims.quote: V organih se smejo za določanje stopenj tajnosti podatkov uporabljati samo stopnje, določene v prejšnjem odstavku.
claims.quote_english: Bodies may use only the levels set out in the preceding paragraph when determining the classification level of data.
claims.title: Zakon o tajnih podatkih (uradno prečiščeno besedilo) (ZTP-UPB2), 13. člen

indicators.research_note: Article 13 of the Classified Information Act (ZTP) defines four statutory levels: STROGO TAJNO, TAJNO, ZAUPNO, INTERNO. In addition, the 2018 Government Decree on Information Security sets binding security classes (Z/C/R) for unclassified information assets.

review.reason: Art. 13 of the Classified Information Act (ZTP-UPB2) contains both quoted passages, which set statutory classification levels that bodies must use.

indicators.research_note: No Slovenian cloud certification requiring immunity from non-EU law (SecNumCloud-type) was found. Checked: Decree on Information Security in State Administration (2018), which only requires ministry approval of public cloud use and limits it to lower security classes, with no certification or immunity criteria; the Ministry of the Interior and Public Administration informatics pages (DRO, security policy). No authoritative statement that no such scheme exists was found either, so unknown rather than no. Web search budget was exhausted, which limited the search for any newer instrument under the information security act.

review.reason: No claims were cited and no source was found either way, so unknown stands.

claims.title: O nas

indicators.research_note: The government PKI root (SI-TRUST Root) and the qualified CAs SIGEN-CA/SIGOV-CA are run by the State Trust Services Centre, part of a ministry (since the 2026 reorganisation, the Ministry of the Interior and Public Administration). The EU Trusted List browser was not fetched because it is JavaScript-rendered.

review.reason: The SI-TRUST 'O nas' page confirms verbatim that SI-TRUST operates within the Ministry of the Interior and Public Administration and runs SI-TRUST Root and the qualified CAs SIGEN-CA and SIGOV-CA.

review.reason: The SI-TRUST pages confirm verbatim that the ministry-run centre is custodian of SI-PASS, the single identity-verification and e-signature point, and issues smsPASS, and that the eID card is issued at state administrative units.

Data-centre addresses and number of sites were not researched further.

review.reason: The ministry sector page confirms verbatim that it manages hardware and software in state data centres at the central DRO site and in local data centres of centralised bodies, which shows state operation today.

claims.quote: zagotavljamo brezhibno delovanje in optimalno uporabniško izkušnjo portala Državnega računalniškega oblaka.

indicators.research_note: The State Computing Cloud (Državni računalniški oblak, DRO) is in operation and hosts government services that handle sensitive and personal data. Ministry sectors run the platform and its self-service portal. The same page says DRO won an innovation award in 2015, so it has been running for about a decade.

review.reason: The gov.si page confirms verbatim that services handling sensitive and personal data run on the established State Computing Cloud (DRO), and the ministry sector page confirms it operates the DRO portal, so it is in operation, not announced.
